summary: This work demonstrates hardware-efficient erasure qubits using the ground and second-excited states of individual superconducting transmon qutrits, with erasure detection via a microwave-activated two-qutrit SWAP gate to an ancilla. Post-selected logical $T_1$ and $T_2$ lifetimes exceed 500 μs and 300 μs respectively—ten times longer than the bare transmon—with single-qubit Clifford gate infidelity of $7.6 \times 10^{-4}$ under erasure detection.
motivation: Erasure qubits convert dominant decoherence errors into detectable leakage, enabling higher fault-tolerance thresholds and better QEC scaling than conventional qubit encodings. Dual-rail implementations require three physical qubits per logical qubit; exploiting the multilevel structure of individual transmons could reduce overhead while remaining compatible with standard superconducting circuit-QED hardware.
method: Three-qubit device with flux-tunable transmons; data qubit $Q_1$ encodes logical states in $|g\rangle$ and $|f\rangle$, with $|e\rangle$ leakage detected via four-wave-mixing-driven $|eg\rangle \leftrightarrow |0_\mathrm{L}f\rangle$ SWAP gate to ancilla $Q_a$. Mid-circuit erasure checks interleaved every 3.52 μs with XY4 dynamical decoupling; post-selection retains only trajectories with no detected erasures.
result: Logical $T_1$ of $549(56)$ μs for $|+Z\rangle$ state and phase-flip coherence of $301(22)$ μs with erasure detection; double-decay and false-negative errors contribute $1.0 \times 10^{-3}$ and $0.9 \times 10^{-3}$ respectively per cycle; erasure lifetime $\sim 45$ μs satisfies the hierarchy of Pauli errors substantially below erasure errors. Two-qubit Bell states between erasure qubits demonstrate ancilla dual-purposing for both erasure detection and parity checking with fidelities up to $0.93(3)$.
